ranch: Rancho San Francisco (later the core of Newhall Ranch / Newhall Land and Farming Company)
county: Northwestern Los Angeles County and eastern Ventura County, California
grant_note: 48,612-acre Mexican land grant made 22 Jan 1839 by Gov. Juan B. Alvarado to Antonio del Valle (a former Spanish/Mexican army officer). Site of the first documented California gold discovery (Francisco Lopez, Placerita Canyon, 6 Mar 1842). Held by the del Valle family, then William Wolfskill; the LA-County portion was purchased 15 Jan 1875 by Henry Mayo Newhall for ~$90,000 and became Newhall Ranch / Newhall Land and Farming Co. after his death in 1882. RANCHO CAMULOS, the ~1,800-acre western portion in VENTURA COUNTY, was retained by the del Valle family as their home ranch (cattle + winery) and is the 'Home of Ramona' of Helen Hunt Jackson's 1884 novel. Grantee/owner families: DEL VALLE (Antonio Seferino, Ygnacio, Reginaldo F., Ysabel Varela), NEWHALL. DISAMBIGUATION: this is NOT the City/County of San Francisco; NOT 'Rancho San Francisco de las Llagas' (Santa Clara County); NOT 'Rancho San Francisquito'. Camulos land WAS part of the original Rancho San Francisco grant, so del Valle/Camulos imagery is on-target for this ranch.
